sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Simulator 8.7 Tab A: DVC Pipeline DAG and Content-Addressed Execution Studio. Click Execute dvc repro to see a clean cache hit, then mutate hyperparameters or raw data to inspect stage invalidation cascades.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Simulator Tab A is live! Try clicking Tune Hyperparams to see Ingestion and Features stay cached in zero seconds while Train and Eval re-execute in 75 seconds!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: In Simulator Tab B, we model cloud GPU compute economics. Adjust the cluster hourly rate, daily runs, and cached fraction sliders to observe 30-day cumulative cost reductions.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Check out the cost curves in Tab B! A 68.8% cached fraction saves nearly 10,000 dollars each month, providing a 3.2x acceleration factor!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 1: An engineer adds an inline comment to features.py. Does the code hash mutate, does the stage fingerprint change, and how do we prevent comment edits from invalidating stages?

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Checkpoint 1! Does SHA-256 care whether text is code or a comment? And how can AST normalizers protect our pipeline cache?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Correct! Cryptographic SHA-256 evaluates raw file bitstreams, so even whitespace or comments mutate the code hash and stage fingerprint, forcing a re-run. AST normalizers or bytecode hashing protect caches.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. SHA-256 does not parse Python syntax; it evaluates raw bitstreams. Any character addition mutates the code hash and stage key, forcing dvc repro to re-execute.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 2: Evaluate our 530-second pipeline under a hyperparameter change on Training versus a bug fix in Ingestion. What are the runtimes and bypassed stages?

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Checkpoint 2! Calculate the execution times: Ingestion is 30 seconds, Preprocessing 180, Training 300, and Evaluation 20. Which stages get bypassed in each case?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Spot on! Case 1 bypasses Ingestion and Preprocessing, executing only Training and Evaluation in 320 seconds and saving 39.6%. Case 2 mutates root Ingestion, cascading through all 4 stages for a full 530-second rerun.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. In Case 1, Ingestion and Preprocessing remain cached, requiring only 320 seconds. In Case 2, root data mutation strictly invalidates all downstream stages for a full 530-second execution.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 3: Dual Formative Verification. Calculate Amdahl's speedup for a 240-minute pipeline with 90% cached, and find the critical path and makespan for the genomic DAG.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Final Capstone Checkpoint! In Part 1, calculate the Amdahl speedup and daily iteration surge. In Part 2, find the critical path among A to B to E, A to C to E, and A to D to E!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Masterclass complete! Part 1: A 90% cached fraction yields a 10x speedup, surging workday throughput from 2 to 11 iterations. Part 2: Path A to C to E is the critical path at 95 minutes, delivering a 1.842x parallel speedup.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. In Part 1, 1 over 1 minus 0.90 is 10x speedup, enabling 11 runs per day. In Part 2, Path A to C to E takes 10 plus 60 plus 25 equals 95 minutes, yielding a 1.842x parallel speedup.
